scenes.title: The last of the sea
scenes.speaker: Rook
text: The track tops a rise and you turn without meaning to. Behind you Skelmed is a smudge of smoke and palisade, and past it the sea, flat and bright and harmless-looking.

greet.text: "Never been further than the hills," Rook says. He doesn't look back. "Ma says Eastmere's got stone walls. Real ones."
[[voice:Endurance]]Forty miles, near enough. Two days, if your legs hold and the road's kind.

choices.label: "We'll be back."
choices.result: [[mood:happy]]"Course we will." He hitches his bow higher on his shoulder. "Someone has to tell her I was right about everything."

choices.label: Turn your back on the sea and walk on

scenes.title: The Brannock ford
text: The road runs down into a river and comes out the other side. The water's brown and quick and knee-deep over flat stones, cold enough to make your teeth ache just looking at it.

greet.text: Rook is already filling his skin. "Last clean water till the farms," he says. "Drink till it hurts."

choices.label: Fill your waterskin, drink, and wade across
choices.result: You drink until your stomach sloshes, fill the skin to bursting, and wade across with your boots round your neck. The cold bites to the bone, then lets go.

scenes.title: An empty farm
scenes.speaker: Rook
text: A farmhouse stands back from the road with its door hanging open. The fields round it have gone to thistle. Someone painted a mark on the gatepost, a crown over a coin, and someone else tried to scrub it off.

greet.text: "Tax mark," Rook says. "Means they couldn't pay. Means the king's men came and took the rest."

choices.label: Search the house
choices.result: Bare boards and a cold hearth. Whoever lived here took what they could carry. In the root cellar you find a sack with a handful of hazelnuts, and mushrooms growing in the damp.

choices.label: "Who were they?"
choices.result: [[mood:sad]]"Dunno. Folk like us." He looks at the scrubbed mark a long time. "That's the thing. They're always folk like us."

scenes.title: Thornby well
text: A huddle of six houses round a well, the first people you've seen since Skelmed. A woman is drawing water and watches you come the way you'd watch a dog you didn't know.

greet.text: "Eastmere road?" she says. "Half a day on. You can fill your skins. Bread's six coppers, if you've got them."

choices.label: Fill your waterskin at the well
choices.result: The well water tastes of iron and cold stone. Better than anything you've ever drunk.

choices.label: Buy a loaf of bread ({price:6})
choices.result: She wraps it in a cloth and doesn't quite smile. "Mind the road after dark. It's not been right this year."

scenes.title: A peddler
scenes.speaker: Peddler
text: A man with a pack the size of a barrel is resting on a milestone, fanning himself with his hat.

greet.text: "Customers! On this road! Sit, sit. Bandages, bread, a little something for the cold. All honest prices, or near enough."

choices.label: "What's the road like ahead?"
choices.result: [[mood:worried]]"Quiet. Too quiet. Used to be you'd pass ten carts a day. Now it's me and the crows, and the crows look at you funny."

choices.label: Wish him well and walk on

scenes.title: People walking west
text: A cart comes the other way, pulled by a man instead of a horse. A woman walks beside it with a baby, and two children ride on top of everything they own.

greet.text: "Don't go to Eastmere," the man says, without stopping. "Or go, see for yourself. We're going to the coast. My brother's in Skelmed."

choices.label: "Skelmed's struggling too."
choices.result: [[mood:sad]]He just nods, like he knew, and keeps pulling. "Then we'll struggle by the sea. At least there's fish."

choices.label: Give them some food
choices.result: The woman takes the loaf with both hands. She doesn't say anything. She doesn't need to.

choices.label: Let them pass and walk on

scenes.title: Something in the grass
text: A patch of mushrooms in the verge.

scenes.title: Round the fire
scenes.speaker: Rook
text: You find a hollow out of the wind and get a fire going. Rook skins nothing, cooks nothing, just sits and feeds sticks into it and watches the dark.

greet.text: "First night I've ever slept out of sight of the sea," he says. "It's too quiet. You can hear yourself think."

choices.label: "Tell me about Ida."
choices.result:
[[mood:happy]]"Ma?" He snorts. "She was a soldier, once. King's archer, back when Melvin was worth fighting for. She won't talk about why she stopped."

[[mood:sad]]"She sent me because she can't leave them. She'll never leave them. That's Ma."

choices.label: "What will you do in Eastmere?"
choices.result: "Find someone in charge. Tell them about the wolves, the levy, all of it." He pokes the fire. "And if no one's listening, find someone who will."

choices.label: "Get some sleep. I'll take first watch."
choices.result: [[mood:happy]]"Wake me if anything's got more than four legs." He's asleep almost before he's finished saying it.

scenes.title: Eastmere
scenes.speaker: Rook
text: The road climbs one last rise and there it is: Eastmere, grey walls on a low hill, smoke from a hundred chimneys, a banner over the gate you can't make out from here.
This is as far as the slice goes for now. Eastmere itself is being built next.

choices.label: Turn around and walk back to Skelmed

scenes.title: The north gate
text: The gate stands open on the road north and east, toward the forest, the hills, and Eastmere two days beyond them.

choices.label: Set off for Eastmere (two days on foot)
